report_name: Congressional Report Finds US Response to Cyberscams 'Fragmented'

identities.name: U.S. Congress
identities.description: The U.S. legislative body whose Joint Economic Committee conducted an investigation into the federal government's response to cyberscams.

identities.name: Joint Economic Committee
identities.description: The congressional committee that authored the report finding the U.S. government's response to cyberscams to be 'dangerously fragmented'.

identities.name: FBI
identities.description: A U.S. federal agency cited in the congressional report for lack of coordination and low recovery rates in combating cyberscams, returning only $336 million of nearly $18 billion lost in 2025.

identities.name: Secret Service
identities.description: A U.S. federal agency mentioned as part of the fragmented government response to cyberscams.

identities.name: State Department
identities.description: A U.S. federal agency criticized in the report for funding cuts that eliminated an anti-scam training program in Bangladesh.

identities.name: Maggie Hassan
identities.description: A U.S. Senator who co-led the Joint Economic Committee investigation into the U.S. response to cyberscams.

identities.name: Don Beyer
identities.description: A U.S. Representative who co-led the Joint Economic Committee investigation into the U.S. response to cyberscams.

identities.name: American public
identities.description: The ultimate victims of the global cyberscams, who lost nearly $18 billion to online fraud in 2025.

identities.name: Private Sector Platforms
identities.description: Private sector entities, such as banks and social media companies, implicated in the report for failing to prevent the abuse of their services for fraud.
